isha-2.translation: Doing your work here, you may wish to live a hundred years. For you there is no other way than this: action does not cling to a person who lives like this.
isha-2.meaning: Live a full life doing your work, in the spirit of the first verse, and your actions will not bind you.
isha-2.explanation: After the opening call to see God in everything and enjoy through letting go, the Isha says one may still work and wish to live a full hundred years. Action done in that spirit does not stain the doer.

isha-3.translation: Those worlds called demonic are covered in blind darkness. Those who kill the Self go there after death.
isha-3.meaning: People who deny or ignore their true Self end up in darkness.
isha-3.explanation: The Isha warns that those who 'kill the Self', living as if the Self did not exist, enter sunless, dark worlds after death. It describes the result of a life cut off from one's own spirit.

isha-4.translation: The One does not move, yet is swifter than the mind. The senses cannot reach it, for it runs ahead. Standing still, it outruns those who run. In it the wind sustains the waters.
isha-4.meaning: The Self is still and yet faster than thought. The senses can never catch it.
isha-4.explanation: The Upanishad describes the Self through paradox. It is unmoving yet faster than the mind; the sense powers (called devas here) can never catch it. Within it the cosmic breath sustains all activity.

isha-5.translation: It moves and it does not move. It is far away and it is near. It is inside all this, and it is outside all this.
isha-5.meaning: God is both moving and still, far and near, inside everything and outside it.
isha-5.explanation: Another set of paradoxes. The Self is beyond categories: it moves yet is still, it is distant yet close, it is within everything and also beyond everything.

isha-6.translation: One who sees all beings in the Self and the Self in all beings no longer shrinks from anyone.
isha-6.meaning: When you see yourself in everyone and everyone in yourself, you stop fearing or disliking others.
isha-6.explanation: This is one of the most quoted verses of the Upanishads. Seeing the one Self in all beings, and all beings in the Self, dissolves fear, disgust and hatred toward others.

keywords.meaning: and the Self in all beings

isha-7.translation: For one who knows, when all beings have become the Self, what delusion or sorrow can there be for one who sees oneness?
isha-7.meaning: When you see that everything is one, there is no room for confusion or sorrow.
isha-7.explanation: For the knower, all beings have become one's own Self. Where everything is seen as one, there is nothing left to be confused about or to grieve over.

isha-8.translation: He has gone everywhere. He is bright, bodiless, without wound or sinew, pure and untouched by evil. He is the seer, the wise, all-encompassing and self-existent. He has set out all things rightly for all time.
isha-8.meaning: The Supreme is pure, bodiless, wise and everywhere, and has ordered all things rightly forever.
isha-8.explanation: The Isha describes the Supreme: radiant, without a body or any flaw, pure and sinless. He is the all-seeing poet and thinker, present everywhere, self-born, who arranged everything properly through endless years.

isha-9.translation: Those who follow ignorance enter blind darkness. Into still greater darkness, as it were, go those who delight only in knowledge.
isha-9.meaning: Ignorance leads to darkness, but pride in mere knowledge can lead to even deeper darkness.
isha-9.explanation: A puzzling verse. Those who pursue only avidya, worldly action and ritual, enter darkness. But those who cling only to vidya, a narrow intellectual knowledge, go into even greater darkness. Both are incomplete alone.

isha-10.translation: They say one result comes from knowledge, and another from ignorance. So we have heard from the wise who explained it to us.
isha-10.meaning: Knowledge and ignorance each lead to their own result, as the wise have taught.
isha-10.explanation: The Upanishad reports what the sages taught: knowledge and ignorance each produce a different outcome.

isha-11.translation: One who knows both knowledge and ignorance together crosses death through ignorance and attains immortality through knowledge.
isha-11.meaning: Use action to get through worldly life, and wisdom to reach the eternal.
isha-11.explanation: The resolution: one must hold both together. Through avidya, meaning action and worldly duty, one passes beyond death; through vidya, spiritual knowledge, one reaches immortality.

isha-12.translation: Those who worship the unmanifest enter blind darkness. Into still greater darkness, as it were, go those who delight only in the manifest.
isha-12.meaning: Clinging only to the unseen, or only to the seen, both lead to darkness.
isha-12.explanation: Parallel to verse nine. Those who worship only asambhuti, the unmanifest cause, enter darkness. Those devoted only to sambhuti, the manifest world, go to greater darkness.

isha-13.translation: They say one result comes from the manifest, and another from the unmanifest. So we have heard from the wise who explained it to us.
isha-13.meaning: The manifest and the unmanifest each lead to their own result, as the wise have taught.
isha-13.explanation: Once more the Upanishad reports the teaching of the sages: the manifest and the unmanifest produce distinct results.

isha-14.translation: One who knows both the manifest and destruction together crosses death through destruction and attains immortality through the manifest.
isha-14.meaning: Understanding both what comes and what passes away leads beyond death to immortality.
isha-14.explanation: As with knowledge and ignorance, the two must be held together. Knowing the perishable, one passes beyond death; knowing the manifest Lord, one gains immortality.

isha-15.translation: The face of truth is covered by a golden disc. Uncover it, Pushan, so that I, who love the truth, may see it.
isha-15.meaning: Truth is hidden behind dazzling things. The seeker prays for the cover to be removed.
isha-15.explanation: The closing verses are a prayer at the time of death. The sun's golden brilliance is pictured as a lid hiding the face of truth. The seeker asks Pushan, the nourishing sun, to remove it.

isha-16.translation: Pushan, sole seer, Yama, Sun, child of Prajapati, spread out your rays and gather your light. I see your most beautiful form. That Person over there, I am he.
isha-16.meaning: The seeker asks the sun to soften its light, and realises: the Person in the sun is my own Self.
isha-16.explanation: The seeker addresses the sun by many names and asks it to withdraw its blinding rays so its gracious form can be seen. Then comes a great realisation: the Person within the sun is the same as oneself.

isha-17.translation: Let my breath return to the immortal wind, and this body end in ashes. Om. Mind, remember. Remember what has been done. Mind, remember. Remember what has been done.
isha-17.meaning: At death the breath joins the wind and the body becomes ash. The mind is asked to remember one's deeds.
isha-17.explanation: A prayer at the moment of death. The life-breath merges into the cosmic wind, the body is cremated. The dying person asks the mind to recall what has been done in life.

isha-18.translation: Agni, lead us by the good path to prosperity, O God who knows all our ways. Keep away from us crooked wrongdoing. We offer you our many words of praise.
isha-18.meaning: A prayer to the fire god: lead us on the right path and keep us from wrongdoing.
isha-18.explanation: The Isha ends with a famous prayer to Agni, the sacred fire, who knows every path. The seeker asks to be led by the good way and protected from deceitful sin, and offers praise.
